475: Built around Repulsor Executioners providing heavy fire support, Marshals and Castellans buffing Sword Brethren and Assault Intercessors pushing forward in transports, with the Emperor's Champion hunting priority targets in melee. The plan is to crack armour at range with skimmer-mounted guns while transported infantry floods midfield objectives, using the Champion's re-roll hits and wounds to guarantee key character or elite kills. It punishes horde-heavy and mid-armour lists through the combination of mass infantry pressure and consistent anti-tank overload from the Repulsor Executioners. However, elite low-model-count armies that can delete the Executioners early leave the infantry unsupported and exposed on objectives with limited scoring punch.
447: Built around Huron Blackheart, Defilers, Masters of the Maelstrom, and Chosen riding in Red Corsairs Raiders transports, this is a mechanized mid-table brawler with a serious gunline backbone. The list wins by using Huron's Dark Pact engine to fuel Chosen and Daemon Princes in melee while Defilers and skimmer-mounted units pound priority targets from range, with Masters of the Maelstrom locking down scoring lanes. It punishes infantry-heavy and lightly-armored lists hard, combining mobile anti-armor from Defilers with Lethal Hits on melee units to overload defensive resources across multiple threat vectors simultaneously. Elite low-volume shooting armies that can surgically delete the transport layer before Chosen disembark will stall the entire threat engine, leaving expensive units stranded and scoring on the wrong side of the board.
461: Built around Rotigus, Great Unclean Ones, and swarms of Plaguebearers, Beasts of Nurgle, and Nurglings operating under the Plague Legion detachment, this is a suffocating horde that buries the table in Nurgle bodies. The win condition is attrition through mandatory Battle-shock: keep multiple Nurgle units within 9" of everything the opponent owns, force cascading Battle-shock tests every Command phase, then let Warptide-boosted Battleline units advance-and-charge while still shooting to grind down a demoralized enemy. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that struggle to stay outside the 9" Shadow of Chaos bubble while weathering wave after wave of layered chip damage. It cracks open against fast, long-range alpha-strike lists that can kill key anchor units before the bubble engulfs them, collapsing the Battle-shock engine before it ever gets rolling.
448: Built around Venomcrawlers, Defilers, Forgefiends, and Maulerfiends, anchored by Vashtorr the Arkifane and a Warpsmith, this is a wall of Daemon Vehicles leaning heavily on Soulforged Warpack's Dark Pact contract to add +1 to Wound on ranged attacks and +2 Attacks in melee simultaneously. The win condition is straightforward brutality: invoke contracts across multiple Daemon Vehicles in the same phase to overload armour saves, using Vashtorr and the Warpsmith to keep the engines operational while Forgefiends strip targets at range and Maulerfiends close for the kill. It punishes elite-armour lists and mechanised forces hard — the wound-roll bonus on ranged attacks means even mid-toughness vehicles get cracked efficiently, and the melee attack spike turns any Maulerfiend or Defiler contact into a wrecking event. The build's fragility is internal: Dark Pacts demand Leadership tests, and cascading failures across multiple vehicles in a single phase can gut the engine's output at exactly the wrong moment.
450: Built around Wyches, Incubi, and Reavers flooding out of Venoms and Raiders, this is a Skysplinter Assault list supplemented by Exhibition of Slaughter — every disembark grants Ignores Cover on ranged and Lance on melee, while Wych Cult units layer on Lethal Hits against non-Monsters and non-Vehicles. The win condition is a coordinated mid-table explosion: park transports at threat range, disembark onto or adjacent to objectives, and delete infantry screens with lance-buffed Incubi and lethal-hitting Wyches before the opponent can respond. It absolutely punishes horde and infantry-heavy lists, where Lethal Hits on melee combined with Ignores Cover shooting turns every disembark into a massacre. Armies that deny the disembark moment — deep strike denial, castle gunlines that kill transports before they arrive, or heavy Monster/Vehicle spam that shrugs the Lethal Hits — can crack the engine before it fires.
466: Built around Infractors and Tormentors riding inside transports, supported by a Lord Exultant, winged Daemon Prince of Slaanesh, Defiler, and Noise Marines, this is a mobile mid-table brawler that threatens armour from multiple angles simultaneously. The engine is the Coterie Of The Conceited pledge mechanic — each round you forecast kills, and hitting that number chains into Pact points that compound your efficiency, turning aggression into a self-reinforcing resource loop. It punishes lists that present multiple exposed vehicles or fragile units because the kill-count pledge rewards exactly that kind of spread damage, and the transport-infantry core can close range fast enough to make the pledge consistently achievable. Bubble-wrap screens and elite single-unit armies crack it open, since both make hitting your pledge number unreliable while weathering your damage output.
473: Built around Paladin Squads, Brotherhood Chaplain, Brotherhood Terminator Squads, and Grand Masters, this is a melee-hammer list running primarily Argent Assault with Banishers as a secondary strat tax. The engine is straightforward: Paladin Squads hit harder against high-Toughness targets via Argent Assault's wound-roll bonus, while Banishers lets fighting units pass Leadership to layer on Sustained Hits 1 or additional melee buffs, and Interceptors provide mobile board presence to score and screen. It punishes low-model-count elite armies by concentrating buffed, high-volume Psychic melee into a single target per phase, overwhelming defensive layers before they can trade back efficiently. However, it sits at a coin-flip winrate, and lists with durable screens, high-AP shooting to strip Terminators before the fight phase, or anything that forces it to fight piecemeal will bleed it dry before its hammers ever land cleanly.
481: Built around the Knight Castellan, Knight Destrier, and a mixed screen of Armiger Warglaives and Helverins, this list pairs the Dominus Foebreakers detachment's +1 to hit against units in terrain with the Gate Warden Lance's defensive line to control both ends of the board simultaneously. The plan is to use the Castellan's overwhelming firepower to punish anything hiding in cover while Armigers pressure objectives and generate attrition the opponent can't ignore. It punishes gunline and castle builds hardest — armies that sit in terrain hand over hit bonuses and get dismantled by Archeotech Autoloaders cycling firepower across the game. Mobile melee threats that close distance quickly and bypass terrain positioning can crack the spacing before the defensive line pays off.
480: Built around Armiger Warglaives and Helverins alongside Knight Castellans and supporting Questoris chassis, this is a mobile combined-arms force that floods the board with medium and heavy Knights rather than committing to a single centerpiece. The plan is to leverage the Armiger swarm as an Oath-cycling engine — particularly under Questoris Companions' ability to chain additional Oaths when current ones resolve — turning sustained pressure into compounding buff states that drive consistent damage output turn after turn. The layered lethality profile punishes mid-range armies that lack dedicated anti-tank overload, since the sheer number of durable chassis forces opponents to spread damage inefficiently across multiple high-wound targets. Where it cracks is against elite shooting lists that can concentrate fire to delete Knights in sequence before Oath chains compound, as 45% win rate signals the build struggles when it can't survive long enough to cash in its engine.
430: Built around Einhyr Hearthguard, Kâhl, and Brôkhyr Thunderkyn supported by Ironkin Steeljacks and Hernkyn Pioneers, this is a mid-board brawler with serious close-range teeth, running primarily under Hearthguard Covenant and frequently pairing it with either Needgaârd or Mercenary Oathband for YP engine fuel. The plan is to crash Hearthguard and Kâhl into the mid-table within 9" where Hearthguard Covenant's wound-reroll kicks in, while Thunderkyn and Steeljacks saturate targets from range and YP accumulation unlocks ability transitions through the Oathband rules. This punishes defensive gunlines that want to hold at distance — the sheer volume of re-roll-supported firepower at close-medium range overloads saves on elite infantry and vehicles alike. Armies that can reliably screen the 9" bubble, deny mid-board presence early, or alpha-strike the Hearthguard before they engage will crack this list, since the wound-reroll engine evaporates the moment the core units are suppressed or killed at range.
482: Built around packs of Armiger Warglaives and Helverins supported by heavier chassis like the Knight Castellan, Crusader, Lancer, and Destrier, this is a full-plate Freeblade Company list that leans on Feel No Pain 6+ and per-turn wound regeneration to make every Knight harder to finish off. The gameplan is to use mobile anti-armour pressure across multiple large threats simultaneously, forcing opponents to overcommit resources to kill individual Knights while the regeneration drip keeps wounded models functional longer than expected. It punishes lists built around moderate-volume anti-tank that expect clean one-shot kills, since no chassis ever quite dies on schedule and the sheer number of independent armoured threats causes target-priority nightmares. Where it cracks is against massed high-volume shooting or mortal wound spam that races ahead of the 1-wound-per-turn regen and overwhelms the 6+ save before it can matter.
456: Built around Canoptek Wraiths, Technomancers, Scarab Swarms, and Illuminor Szeras, this is a mobile Canoptek swarm engine that floods the board with fast, durable bodies backed by layered reanimation support from the Canoptek Reanimator. The win condition is board control through relentless presence — Wraiths threaten every flank while Scarabs screen and contest, with the C'tan Shard of the Deceiver providing a hard-to-shift anchor that punishes reactive opponents. The +1 to Hit from Awakened Dynasty leadership makes Wraith-led combat punches surprisingly lethal against mid-toughness infantry hordes that expect to trade efficiently into Necron units. The list cracks when faced with high-volume anti-horde shooting or alpha strikes that strip Technomancer babysitters before reanimation can fire, leaving Wraith blobs without their sustain loop.
486: Built around massive Boyz blobs supported by Painboys, Warbosses, and Bigbosses, this is Green Tide in its most literal form — cheap bodies in overwhelming numbers crammed into transports and launched at the midboard. The win condition is grinding opponents off objectives through sheer attrition: Boyz units of 10+ models leverage their 5+ invulnerable save to stay on points while Painboys keep them ticking, and Stormboyz hitting BATTLELINE status floods secondary scoring without sacrificing action eligibility during advance or fall-back moves. It punishes elite low-model-count lists brutally, as anti-tank or high-AP shooting gets diluted across dozens of wounds that now save on 5s. However, massed mortal wounds, high-volume low-AP firepower, or deep strike harassment that fragments the blobs before they reach combat size strips the invulnerable threshold and collapses the entire durability engine simultaneously.
487: Built around Mozrog Skragbad, Beastbosses, Squighog Boyz, Beast Snagga Boyz, and Kill Rigs, this list runs Da Big Hunt with an optional Rollin' Deff secondary, delivering a wall of Beast Snagga bodies backed by monster trucks. The engine is Da Big Hunt's Prey designation: every Command phase you lock a target — enemy monster, vehicle, or character — and your entire Beast Snagga force gets charge re-rolls into it, letting you chain-delete priority threats while Gretchin babysit home objectives. It punishes elite armor-light lists that can't handle simultaneous threats from multiple hard-hitting melee units converging with advance-and-charge mobility. It cracks when faced with deep firepower that thins the Beast Snagga screen before the charge, neutralizing the Prey buff before it pays off.
468: Built around Vulkan He'stan, Adrax Agatone, Infernus Squads riding Land Raider Redeemers, and a Librarian support core running Forgefather's Seekers and Librarius Conclave, this is a close-range fire army that weaponises flame at scale. The win condition is delivering Infernus Squads via transport, triggering Seeker's Companions to let them action-and-shoot, then torching mid-board objectives while the Forgefather's Seekers +1 Strength within 12" turns already-dangerous weapons into anti-armour tools. It punishes infantry-heavy lists brutally — massed bodies simply evaporate under high-volume, Strength-buffed assault-enabled flame, and Divination or Pyromancy discipline cycling keeps the kill chain reliable round after round. The build cracks when opponents screen the Land Raider approaches effectively or apply long-range anti-tank before the Redeemers deliver their cargo, leaving the Infernus Squads stranded outside their lethal 12" threat window.
488: Built around multiple Big Meks with Shokk Attack Guns, Lootas, and Tankbustas hauled forward in Trukks, this is a Dread Mob gunline that leans hard on Mek and Walker units rolling for variable weapon buffs each phase to keep opponents guessing. The plan is to park Gretchin screens on objectives while Trukks deliver Tankbustas into melta range and Shokk Attack Guns crack heavy targets from mid-table, with Gitfinder Gogglez sharpening the key shooter's accuracy and Waaagh!-fueled Sustained Hits 1 turning Loota volleys into a serious threat against infantry blobs. It punishes slow, static armoured lists that can't close the distance quickly, getting overloaded by anti-tank from multiple angles simultaneously. Aggressive fast armies that can strip the Gretchin screens early expose the Meks before they generate enough shooting value, cracking the list open before it stabilizes.
467: Built around Marneus Calgar in the Armour of Antilochus, Victrix Honour Guard, Repulsor Executioners, and Ballistus Dreadnoughts, this is a heavily armoured Ultramarines gunline running the Blade of Ultramar detachment. The plan is to cycle Combat Doctrines across three phases — and recycle them via Calgar — to keep the right buff active while Repulsor Executioners and Ballistus Dreadnoughts hammer high-value targets from range, with Scouts and Intercessors holding ground cheaply. It punishes slower armoured lists through sheer sustained firepower, stacking skimmer mobility with heavy anti-armour to outrange and overwhelm single-threat armies. It cracks when fast aggressive lists close the gap before Doctrine cycling pays off, stripping the infantry screens and leaving Calgar's expensive bubble exposed.
478: Built around Thunderwolf Cavalry, Wulfen with storm shields, and Bjorn the Fell-Handed anchoring the character core, this list layers hard-hitting melee hammers over a chassis of Gladiator Lancers, Iron Priests, and Fenrisian Wolf screens. The plan is to grind the mid-table with Wulfen and Thunderwolves while Gladiator Lancers strip armour at range, using mass bodies and transport infantry to saturate objectives and force unfavorable trades. It punishes slower, elite armies that can't handle simultaneous threats across multiple lanes — the combination of mobile melee pressure and skimmer-based anti-armour overloads target priority. However, the build lacks a single dominant detachment identity, leaving it inconsistent at the top end, and focused elite shooting or alpha-strike lists that delete the cavalry before they engage will crack the engine entirely.
428: Built around Riptides, Broadsides, Stealth Battlesuits, and Pathfinder-guided screening, Mont'Ka turns every unit into a mobile firebase by granting [ASSAULT] to all ranged weapons for the first three battle rounds, letting heavy platforms shoot after advancing without penalty. The engine is Guided fire: Pathfinders tag priority targets so the Riptides and Broadsides hit with [LETHAL HITS], compressing armour saves and fishing for mortal-equivalent wounds against high-toughness vehicles early while Piranhas and Stealth Suits harass and screen. It punishes armour-heavy lists hard — the mobile anti-armour axis combined with Guided [LETHAL HITS] creates disproportionate damage output against multi-wound, high-save targets before they can entrench. Anything that kills the Pathfinder screen early collapses the Guided synergy, and without [LETHAL HITS] the damage output drops sharply against elite infantry.
483: Built around a Broodlord-led Genestealer swarm backed by Lictors, Neurolictors, Von Ryan's Leapers, and Deathleaper, this list runs Vanguard Onslaught — making Deathleaper eligible as Warlord — and Ambush Predators to give the entire assassination package Deep Strike alongside re-rolls to hit against Characters. The win condition is a layered infiltration pressure game: mass Genestealers swamp midboard objectives while Lictors and Neurolictors deep strike into backfield Characters, stripping command assets and denying reinforcement plays. It punishes elite, low-model-count lists badly, overwhelming their screen with horde volume and threatening every exposed Character simultaneously. Against armies with dense cheap screens and strong shooting, the melee-only engine bleeds models before it can close, and the Deep Strike units arrive too late to recover ground.
490: Built around Tzaangor Enlightened as the primary damage engine, backed by Sekhetar Robots buffed through the Sekhetar Cohort's Infusion aura giving their melee attacks +1 WS and the [PSYCHIC] keyword, with Sorcerers, Tzaangor Shamans, and a winged Daemon Prince providing layered psychic support across a large horde footprint. The plan is to flood mid-table early using mass bodies to control No Man's Land objective markers, unlocking the Hexwarp Thrallband's Flow of Magic across the entire centre and amplifying psychic weapons across the army while the Enlightened and Robots deliver punishing close-range kill chains. This build punishes slower gunlines and low-model-count elite armies that cannot efficiently trade into a mass-horde psychic threat profile without being overrun on objectives simultaneously. It cracks open when fast, aggressive lists deny the No Man's Land control window early, collapsing the Flow of Magic engine before the Robots and Enlightened can close distance under its coverage.
489: Built around Scarab Occult Terminators, Rubric Marines, Sekhetar Robots, and a Sorcerer in Terminator Armour leading the core, with Tzaangor Enlightened and Tzaangors providing mass bodies across the board. The plan is to flood objectives with near-unkillable infantry blobs while the Terminators and Robots drive up the midfield as a brawling hammer, layering Psychic shooting from Enlightened bows and Rubrics to grind out attrition kills and bank secondaries through sheer presence. Where Grand Coven appears, Imbued Manifestation extends that Psychic ranged threat to punishing distances, amplifying the gunline pressure. Concentrated high-damage alpha strikes or elite melee that bypasses the layered saves can crack this — the build bleeds points when the front line collapses before the bodies can score.
427: Built around Pathfinder Teams, Stealth Battlesuits, Commander in Coldstar, Crisis Starscythe and Fireknife Battlesuits, and a Riptide, this is a two-detachment mobile gunline that keeps cheap units perpetually hidden while its battlesuit core closes distance to punish. The engine is Advanced Acquisition Cadre keeping Pathfinders and Stealth Suits shooting without breaking hidden status, while Retaliation Cadre Battlesuits crash inside 12"—and ideally 9"—to spike Strength and AP on every attack, turning Crisis and Riptide shooting into a close-range blender. It absolutely shreds armored lists and elite infantry by overloading high-toughness targets with improved AP within engagement range, rewarding the player who can dictate the fight's distance. It cracks under pressure from fast melee armies that can rush the battlesuit bubble before the AP bonuses come online, and anything that strips hidden status or screens the midboard denies the close-range prerequisite the whole kill chain depends on.
484:
Built around Psychophages, Pyrovores, a Haruspex, and a Norn Assimilator, this is a mid-table brawler that pairs close-range lethality with the Assimilation Swarm's Harvester regeneration loop — returning wounds and slain Infantry models to key units each Command phase to grind opponents down through sustained attrition.

The win condition is board control through unkillable presence: stack regeneration on durable monsters like the Haruspex and Norn Assimilator, use Ripper Swarms as cheap objective holders, and let the Psychophages and Pyrovores punish anyone who tries to contest midfield at close range.

It punishes slow, durable gunlines that expect to trade efficiently, because the regeneration engine keeps negating that math across multiple turns.

It cracks against fast alpha-strike lists that can isolate and delete key Harvesters before the regeneration cycle stabilises, stripping the engine before it pays off.
500: Built around waves of Purestrain Genestealers and Neophyte Hybrids backed by Achilles Ridgerunners, Reductus Saboteurs, and Atalan Jackals, this list floods the table with bodies across a gunline-and-melee hybrid shell, most commonly under Xenocult Masses. The engine is layered threat saturation: Ridgerunners and Saboteurs suppress and soften targets at range while Purestrains crash into weakened units in melee, with Neophyte Hybrids healing 3 wounds per Command phase inside terrain to sustain the screening base. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that cannot adequately answer both the mobile anti-armour pressure and the melee swarm simultaneously, forcing impossible priority splits. However, high-volume mortal wound output or mass blast weapons that ignore saves by sheer volume can gut the horde core before the Purestrains ever reach their targets.
518: Built around Lokhust Destroyers, Skorpekh Destroyers, Ophydian Destroyers, and their paired Lords, this is a Cursed Legion list that weaponizes the detachment's Strength-stacking engine across every branch of the Destroyer Cult keyword simultaneously. The plan is to trigger the cascade buff — kill or half-strength a unit with one Destroyer unit, then immediately punch through harder targets with the remaining units benefiting from the additional +2 Strength that same turn, chaining activations to dismantle multiple threats in a single phase. It punishes mid-toughness elite armies that lack layered screening, since boosted Strength values push Lokhust shooting and Skorpekh melee into damage brackets those lists simply can't absorb. However, armies that spread across the board with cheap chaff deny the kill-trigger chain, and deep-striking Tomb Blades aside, the list bleeds if opponents contest early before the Strength cascade comes online.
503: Built around Terminator Assault Squads, Terminator Squads, and Librarians in Terminator Armour, this list leverages the Librarius Conclave's round-by-round Psychic Discipline selection to flex between Divination's hit/wound re-rolls when brawling, Biomancy's movement buff to close distance, or Pyromancy's ranged threat — all tuned to whatever the matchup demands. The win condition is delivering massed Terminators into midfield under a chosen Discipline while Darnath Lysander and the Ancient provide durability and combat punch, scoring through sheer attrition dominance on objectives. It punishes elite infantry lists that expect to trade evenly in melee, because stacking re-rolls and AP across a wall of 2+ saves creates wildly unfavorable exchanges. It cracks under massed low-AP shooting or deep-strike alpha strikes that strip bodies before the Disciplines can compound — Terminators are durable but slow enough that a well-placed screen or deployment denial can strand them off objectives entirely.
517: Built around Doomsday Arks, the Silent King, Canoptek Wraiths, and Tomb Blades, this is a mobile ranged-threat army that leverages the Starshatter Arsenal's Assault rule on Vehicle and Mounted weapons — letting Doomsday Arks and Tomb Blades shoot after advancing and still contest objectives. The win condition is objective presence converted into firepower: the detachment's +1 to Hit on attacks targeting units near objectives means every unit contesting a marker is also a priority kill target your opponent cannot safely ignore, while Flayed Ones and Wraiths apply close-range pressure to force bad trades. Chrono-impedance Fields on the Wraiths creates a screen-and-deny layer that punishes aggressive melee armies who want to rush your shooting base. The weakness is consistency — at roughly even win rates, the list struggles against armies that can either deny objective presence entirely through deep strike denial or simply outrange the Doomsday Arks before the Assault bonus ever comes online.
504: Built around Land Speeders and Storm Speeder Hammerstrikes as the core strike package, supported by Vindicators, Eradicators with heavy bolters, and Incursors providing screening infantry, with the Fulguris Task Force granting Speeders an ingress move in the first Movement phase to reposition aggressively from turn one. The plan is to weaponize that first-turn ingress to drop the Speeder hammer into optimal anti-armour range immediately while Vindicators and Eradicators bracket mid-field threats, scoring through board pressure and eliminating heavy anchor units opponents need to hold objectives. It punishes armour-heavy and vehicle-dense lists hard, overloading them with redundant high-damage mobile platforms that are difficult to prioritize simultaneously. Dedicated counter-screening and fast melee can crack it open, since the Incursor screen is relatively thin and losing Speeder bodies early deflates the entire kill chain.
530: Built around Vertus Praetors, Allarus Custodians, and Shield-Captains pushing isolated units into the Lions Of The Emperor bonus — add 1 to Hit and Wound whenever no friendly unit sits within 6" — this list leans hard into spread-out, self-sufficient combat nodes ferried forward in transports. The win condition is board saturation: each isolated unit becomes a precision kill-piece that can delete priority targets through boosted hit-and-wound chains, while Witchseekers fill screening roles that free the heavy hitters to operate alone. It punishes low-model elite armies that can't contest every isolated threat simultaneously, overloading defenders with multiple dangerous vectors they lack the bodies to screen. Dense horde lists or anything that floods the midboard with cheap chaff can collapse the isolation requirement, forcing units into proximity and shutting off the core detachment bonus entirely.
525: Built around Land Speeder Vengeances, Ravenwing Black Knights, and Outrider Squads, this is a hypermobile Dark Angels cavalry-and-skimmer list running Company Of Hunters, which lets all Adeptus Astartes units shoot after Advancing or Falling Back, and Mounted units shoot and charge after doing the same. The plan is to flood every angle simultaneously — skimmers lay down heavy fire from wherever they need to be, Black Knights crash charges after Advancing, and Outriders (now Battleline) hold objectives while still shooting. It punishes slow gunlines and anything relying on positional cover, since Darkflight Pursuit strips cover saves from all Ravenwing Fly units' ranged attacks, turning defended terrain into a non-factor. Dense melee armies that can lock the skimmers in combat and deny the Advance-and-shoot engine — preventing the list from freely repositioning — are its biggest threat.
527: Built around Nekrosor Ammentar, a Lokhust Lord, and blobs of Lokhust Destroyers supported by Canoptek Wraiths and a Skorpekh Lord, this Awakened Dynasty list uses the detachment's +1 to Hit while a CHARACTER leads a unit to make its destroyer packages brutally accurate. The core engine is Nekrosor buffing Lokhust Destroyers into near-guaranteed hit rolls, then leaning on Veil of Darkness to teleport that kill-stack wherever the opponent least wants it mid-game while Wraiths and Reanimators keep bodies on objectives. It punishes elite, low-model-count armies that can't absorb the reroll-efficient, high-accuracy shooting from multiple independent Destroyer threats. Horde armies that flood the board can dilute the teleport threat and screen out the kill zones before Nekrosor's package can redeploy effectively.
522: Built around Berehk Stornbröw leading massed Cthonian Beserks alongside Einhyr Hearthguard, Sagitaurs, and a Hekaton Land Fortress, this list plays a brutal mid-table brawl backed by serious gunline weight. The win condition is getting Beserks into melee contact while Sagitaurs and the Hekaton suppress enemy responses, with the Hearthguard Covenant's re-roll wounds within 9" amplifying close-range devastation into a reliable kill chain. It punishes elite infantry and mid-cost armies that can't handle simultaneous melee pressure and layered vehicle fire, forcing painful priority splits. Spread across multiple detachments with no single dominant anchor, it lacks consistency — armies that screen aggressively to deny the 9" wound re-roll bubble or neutralize the Beserks before contact can collapse the scoring engine entirely.
529: Built around Wolf Guard Headtakers, Wolf Guard Terminators, and Logan Grimnar, this is a transport-heavy assault list running Saga of the Beastslayer to give every Adeptus Astartes model Lethal Hits against Characters, Monsters, and Vehicles — or against all targets once the Saga threshold is met. The win condition is cracking open armored and elite targets early to complete the Saga, then flooding the midfield with Blood Claws and Grey Hunters out of transports while the kill chain snowballs. It punishes lists built around expensive Characters and Vehicles, as Lethal Hits dramatically amplifies wound conversion against exactly those targets. It struggles against horde armies that never present valid Saga targets and can body-block transports from reaching the midfield engagement it needs.
521: Built around Riptides, Crisis Starscythes, Crisis Sunforges, and a Coldstar Commander, with Stealth Battlesuits and Pathfinders providing board presence and marker support. The plan is to close distance aggressively — Retaliation Cadre's short-range buffs reward getting inside 12" and 9" to spike Strength and AP on battlesuit weapons, turning already-punishing firepower into armour-cracking volleys while the Coldstar repositions the kill chain each turn. It punishes elite-armour lists hard, stacking anti-tank overload through multiple medium-to-heavy battlesuit platforms that all benefit from the same proximity buffs simultaneously. Sprawling horde armies and screen-heavy builds can absorb the focused shooting before the battlesuits close to optimal range, and anything that alpha-strikes the mid-table Crisis suits before they engage effectively collapses the entire damage engine.
566:
Built around Arco-Flagellants, Celestian Insidiants, and the Triumph of Saint Katherine, this is a mass-infantry swarm that leans hard into Hallowed Martyrs — the detachment that rewards taking casualties by adding to Hit and Wound rolls, turning attrition into a damage amplifier.

The plan is to flood the board with cheap, punishing bodies, let the Arco-Flagellants and Insidiants absorb punishment until they drop below Starting Strength, then weaponize the Hallowed Martyrs bonus to hit and wound harder than a fresh unit would, with Ministorum Priests and the Triumph stacking further buffs onto already-dangerous units.

It punishes low-volume, elite-model lists that can't clear hordes fast enough — opponents who can't shoot the whole swarm off objectives hand over free Martyrs triggers while bleeding primaries.

It cracks apart against high-volume shooting that deletes units cleanly before they fall below half-strength, denying the wound-roll bonus entirely and collapsing the scoring engine before it fires.
441: Built around Azrael, Deathwing Knights, Inner Circle Companions, and a Librarian cycling Psychic Disciplines each round, this is a transported elite infantry force backed by Land Speeder Vengeances providing skimmer-based fire support. The win condition is delivering hammer units into melee under Azrael's protection while the Librarian's rotating disciplines amplify offense or resilience turn-by-turn, with Vowed objective mechanics across multiple detachments generating sustained primary score. It punishes low-model elite armies that can't contest objectives efficiently, as stacked OC from enhanced Companions and Battle-shocked immunity turns even contested markers into clean holds. However, it folds to mass-model hordes and saturation shooting that overwhelms the limited wound pool of its expensive infantry core before the melee engine ever connects.
550:
Built around Lord of Change, Kairos Fateweaver, Be'lakor, and swarms of Screamers and Flamers, this list runs primarily Scintillating Legion with its Flux token re-roll engine as the core consistency tool, layering in Lords of the Warp and Warptide support detachments across variants.

The plan is to flood multiple angles simultaneously — Screamers threatening mobile anti-armour sweeps while Flamers deliver layered lethal output — spending Flux tokens to force through critical wound or damage rolls at decisive moments rather than relying on raw probability.

It punishes armies with low model counts and moderate saves, where the combination of relentless re-roll access and multi-vector pressure prevents effective screening against the daemon swarms.

Highly concentrated opposing firepower that can delete the Lords of Change and Kairos early cracks this list open, since the entire re-roll and leadership scaffolding collapses without those anchor characters on the table.
551: Built around Bloodcrushers, Bloodletters, and a Rendmaster on Blood Throne supported by a Bloodthirster, this is a pure Khorne daemon tide running Blood Legion or Shadow Legion as its detachment spine. The win condition is simple and brutal: bait or advance enemy units within 6" to trigger Blood Legion's Surge move reactive charges, crashing Bloodcrushers and Flesh Hounds into exposed screens and scoring through melee dominance and board flooding. The layered Lethal Hits across virtually every unit punishes mid-toughness infantry hordes and lightly armoured elite armies that can't screen their advance moves cleanly. However, disciplined opponents who deny the Surge trigger by holding position or deep-striking past the threat bubble leave this list fighting uphill on points, with limited shooting to punish static gunlines.
445: Built around Death Company Marines with Jump Packs, Death Company Dreadnoughts, and Sanguinary Guard led by Lemartes and Astorath, this is a Rage-Cursed Onslaught murder-blob that crashes into enemy lines from above. The win condition is pure melee attrition — charge everything, trigger the detachment's +1 Attacks on charge (or +2 if Battle-shocked), and let re-rolling wound 1s compound the damage output across multiple elite melee units hitting simultaneously. It punishes static gunlines and low-model-count elite armies that can't absorb repeated high-volume melee waves from jump-mobile units arriving from multiple angles. It cracks open against fast screen-and-deny lists or armies that can selectively pick off Lemartes and Astorath before the charge lands, gutting the aura synergy that makes the damage engine function.
459: Built around Scout Sentinels projecting Signal Flares across the board, supported by Rogal Dorn Commanders, Hellhounds, Leman Russ Vanquishers, and a Tech-Priest Enginseer keeping the armour running, this is a Designation Force gunline that uses forward Sentinel spotting to enable heavy vehicle firepower from range. The core engine is Signal Flares: Sentinels push up early, designate targets, and the armoured column deletes priority threats while Gaunt's Ghosts handle infantry screening and objective pressure. The Steel Hammer detachment means Titanic and Squadron units can fire into engagements, punishing melee armies that try to tie up the tanks and giving the gunline an answer to screens wrapping key vehicles. Where it cracks is against fast, mobile armies that can isolate and kill the fragile Sentinels before they flare, shutting down the designation engine and leaving the gunline firing cold.
465: Built around Daemonettes packed into transports, Fiends, a Keeper of Secrets, and a Lord Exultant, this is a mobile mid-table brawler that weaponizes the Carnival of Excess Empowered state — mutual proximity between Emperor's Children and Legions of Excess units triggers Sustained Hits 1 across the board, turning volume-fire infantry into a blender. The plan is to surge transports forward, disembark Daemonettes into the Empowered bubble, and grind opponents off objectives through sheer attack volume while Defilers and mobile anti-armour elements crack open harder targets. It punishes horde armies and anything that wants to sit mid-table, where the Sustained Hits 1 engine compounds already-high attack counts into devastating output. Anything that can strip the Empowered bubble by killing the support units at range, or hard alpha-strike the transports before they unload, collapses the synergy the entire list depends on.
534: Built around Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, Hearthkyn Warriors, and Sagitaurs supported by a Hekaton Land Fortress and an Arkanyst Evaluator, this list blends a grinding midfield brawl with a punishing heavy gunline. The win condition is YP accumulation — destroying enemies fuels the Judgement Points engine, unlocking escalating bonuses that compound across every subsequent turn — while Sagitaurs push forward under Scouts 6" to contest early and force trades on favorable terms. It punishes elite low-model-count armies hardest, where every destroyed unit nets YP efficiently and the Thunderkyn's concentrated heavy firepower can systematically dismantle expensive targets. Horde spam and high-volume cheap units crack it open by diluting the YP-per-kill value and overwhelming the midfield before the engine reaches critical mass.
546: Built around multiple C'tan Shards — Transcendent, Nightbringer, Deceiver, and Void Dragon — supported by Flayed Ones and Hexmark Destroyers, this list runs Pantheon of Woe to wrap its Monster keyword into a force multiplier. The Distortion Fields aura degrades enemy armour saves within 6", letting the C'tan's naturally powerful melee and shooting punch through elite targets while the build repositions aggressively each phase to keep enemies inside that bubble. It punishes durable, low-volume armies — heavily armoured vehicles and multi-wound infantry — where the AP-improvement compounds across every attack from multiple Monsters simultaneously. However, spread-out objective play and high model-count screens force the C'tan to either overcommit into unfavorable engagements or cede the board state, since the aura requires proximity to function.
544: Built around a Skorpekh Lord leading Skorpekh Destroyers, supported by Lokhust Heavy Destroyers, the C'tan Shard of the Void Dragon, and characters Nekrosor Ammentar and Illuminor Szeras, this is a mobile, multi-threat Necron force operating under Awakened Dynasty's +1 to Hit while a Character leads a unit. The win condition is delivering character-buffed Skorpekh units into mid-board threats while Lokhust Heavy Destroyers and the Void Dragon crack armor from range, with Enaegic Dermal Bond keeping the key kill-piece alive long enough to score through attrition. It punishes lists with dispersed, medium-durability infantry by layering lethal melee and ranged anti-armor across multiple vectors simultaneously, forcing impossible priority choices. It cracks open against elite gunlines that can isolate and delete the Skorpekh package before the characters compound its hitting power, stranding the rest of the force without the critical Hit buff.
526: Built around Lokhust Destroyers buffed by a Lokhust Lord, Ophydian Destroyers and Skorpekh Destroyers crashing in on flanks, and Nekrosor Ammentar and Skorpekh Lord layering melee pressure, this list fields overlapping Destroyer threats across every phase. The win condition is threat saturation — the Lokhust Lord's command presence amplifies ranged output while Ophydians tunnel forward and Skorpekh units pin and grind, forcing opponents to address multiple kill vectors simultaneously rather than screen any single one. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that can't cover multiple angles, since the mobile toolbox of ranged and melee Destroyers overwhelms piecemeal defensive positioning. It cracks open against lists that can isolate and delete the Lokhust Lord early, collapsing the ranged chain, or that bring durable screen-and-deny infantry dense enough to absorb the Ophydian and Skorpekh charges before they reach priority targets.
556: Built around Beast Snagga Boyz, Squighog Boyz, and a Beastboss leading mobs of Boyz and Gretchin screens, this is a War Horde list that floods the midboard with bodies and melee violence. The engine is straightforward: War Horde's Sustained Hits 1 on all Ork melee weapons inflates output across every combat, letting sheer volume of attacks from Beast Snagga Boyz and Squighog Boyz grind through anything that doesn't clear the board fast. It punishes low-model-count elite lists that can't efficiently answer multiple large threatening units simultaneously, forcing target-priority nightmares while Gretchin hold backfield objectives. It cracks open when faced with mass high-AP shooting that deletes mobs before they close distance, since the entire plan collapses without melee contact.
558: Built around Warbikers, Deffkoptas, and Deffkilla Wartrikes led by Wazdakka Gutsmek, this is a Kult of Speed wall of fast, durable Speed Freeks that can shoot and charge after Advancing or Falling Back, giving the whole army persistent aggression with no movement tax. The plan is to flood the mid-table early, brawl through whatever holds objectives, and use the advance-and-shoot rule to maintain fire pressure while grinding in melee across multiple turns. It punishes slow, static armies that can't reposition — the ability to Advance and still shoot and charge means defensive bubble-wraps and screen-and-deny tactics are steadily dismantled without giving up tempo. Elite low-volume anti-horde lists crack it open, because the durability here is spread across quantity rather than quality, and anything that removes models faster than the swarm can contest leaves objectives naked.
557: Built around Mozrog Skragbad, the Beastboss, Squighog Boyz, Beast Snagga Boyz, Kill Rig, and thick screens of Gretchin and Boyz, this is a mounted beast-riding horde that floods the midboard with bodies and hits hard in melee. The plan is to crash a wall of cheap screens into the midfield while the Squighog Boyz and Kill Rig deliver lethal combat payloads, trading bodies efficiently and contesting objectives through sheer volume. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that struggle to remove enough wounds before the Squigbeasts are already in their lines, bleeding them dry on secondaries and primary simultaneously. It cracks open against armies with reliable high-volume mortal wound output or consistent blast weapons that can strip the horde screens before the heavy hitters arrive, leaving the kill pieces isolated and exposed.
553: Built around Marneus Calgar, Victrix Honour Guard, and Bladeguard Veterans backed by Repulsor Executioners and a thick screen of Scouts and Intercessors, this list blends a hard-hitting melee hammer with a persistent heavy gunline. The plan is to park on objectives, leverage the Reclamation Force's AP improvement on melee attacks to shred elite infantry in the mid-board while Repulsor Executioners and skimmer fire grind down armour and vehicles at range. It punishes slow, durable lists that want to hold ground — the combination of mobile anti-armour shooting and Calgar's melee threat on objectives makes turtling suicidal. Against fast alpha-strike armies that can strip the screening infantry early and isolate the melee core before it engages, the list struggles to recover.
533: Built around Commander in Coldstar Battlesuit, Crisis Sunforge Battlesuits, and Stealth Battlesuits, this list exploits the Experimental Prototype Cadre's +6" range extension on Battlesuit Characters to threaten targets from punishing distances while Kroot Carnivores and Vespid Stingwings clog mid-table. The win condition is sustained mobile anti-armour pressure — Coldstar and Sunforge units strip hard targets from safe range while Pathfinders spot for Guided fire, with Kauyon kicking in rounds three through five to add Sustained Hits 1 and strip wound-roll modifiers on Spotted units, accelerating the late-game kill rate. It punishes slow, low-mobility armour lists that cannot close the extended engagement envelope before the Kauyon payoff arrives. It cracks under aggressive early-round alpha strikes that collapse the screening infantry before Kauyon activates, leaving the Battlesuits exposed without the sustained fire bonus they depend on.
561: Built around Rubric Marines, Scarab Occult Terminators, and a Sorcerer in Terminator Armour, this is a dense infantry phalanx leaning hard into the Rubricae Phalanx detachment's damage-1 save buff — unmodified Damage 1 attacks get an additional armour save on every Rubricae model, making chip-damage shooting largely irrelevant against the core battleline. The plan is to advance a layered wall of near-unkillable infantry into the midboard, hold objectives through sheer durability, and grind opponents down with massed bolter fire and Terminator close-combat pressure while the Sorcerers stack psychic buffs. It absolutely punishes armies built around high-volume, low-damage shooting — bolt-spam, small-arms chaff clear, or mortal-wound-light gunlines simply bounce off the massed saves. However, concentrated high-damage multi-wound attacks, anti-infantry overload with weapons above Damage 1, and anything that forces the slow-moving mass off objectives before it can entrench will crack the formation wide open.
560: Built around Sekhetar Robots, Rubric Marines, Scarab Occult Terminators, and Sorcerers anchoring a psychic-heavy infantry core, this Hexwarp Thrallband list runs a layered battleforce that expands its Flow of Magic by contesting No Man's Land objectives early, unlocking psychic bonuses across the whole mid-table. The win condition is a cumulative pressure engine: Robots gain +1 WS from Psyker Infusion auras while Rubrics and Terminators grind through Rituals that heal D3 wounds via Ritual of Regeneration, creating a self-sustaining attrition loop that scores through staying power rather than burst damage. It punishes elite low-volume armies that can't strip wounds fast enough across multiple durable Psychic infantry bricks simultaneously. It cracks open against high-mobility deep-strike threats or mass-volume shooting that overwhelms the healing loop before Flow of Magic coverage is established.
514: Built around Tyranid Primes buffing hordes of Hormagaunts and Tyranid Warriors, supported by Hive Guard shooting and Biovore harassment, this list leans into either Subterranean Assault's burrowing Trygons as Character-upgraded flanking threats or Invasion Fleet's Hyper-adaptations for combat tuning. The win condition is board-wide pressure — Primes amplify Hormagaunt and Warrior combat output while underground units erupt into unexpected angles, forcing opponents to defend everywhere simultaneously. It punishes static gunlines and low-model-count armies that can't contest multiple threat vectors at once, particularly when burrowing units surface to collapse flanks the opponent left thin. Elite, low-activation lists that delete key synergy pieces early — especially the Tyranid Primes — collapse the buff chain and leave the swarm directionless.
573: Built around Assault Intercessors, Bladeguard Veterans, and a dense character suite of Sanguinary Priest, Chaplain, and Librarian, this list runs primarily in the Liberator Assault Group, which adds +2 Strength and +1 Attack to every charging Adeptus Astartes unit's melee weapons. The plan is to surge infantry out of transports, trigger Liberator Assault Group's charge bonus across multiple units simultaneously, and delete priority targets in a single fight phase while Baal Predators provide skimmer fire support to clear screens and soften armour. It punishes mid-table melee factions and infantry-heavy lists that can't disengage fast enough once the charge train arrives, turning every activation into an overloaded attack spike. The weakness is that the engine is entirely charge-dependent — anything that denies charges through screen-and-deny, long-range alpha strike, or keeps it at arm's length collapses the whole damage output before the buffs ever trigger.
571: Built around Skorpius Disintegrators, Ironstrider Ballistarii, and infantry screens of Skitarii Rangers, Serberys Raiders, and Sicarian Infiltrators, this castle anchors a heavy gunline behind layered bodies that buy the vehicles repeated shooting windows. The engine is sustained skimmer fire supplemented by Baffling Data Screed forcing enemy vehicles into saves they can't afford, while screened infantry hold objectives and deny deep strike lanes long enough for the guns to dismantle threats piecemeal. It punishes slow armored lists that present clean vehicle targets at range, stacking layered lethality through overlapping fire before the opponent can close and neutralize the Disintegrators. Highly mobile or alpha-strike armies that can bypass the infantry screen and reach the vehicles early crack it open, as the castle collapses quickly once its protected shooting base is disrupted.
577: Built around Eldrad Unseen (implied by name), Warlock Skyrunners, Warlock Conclaves, Wraithlords, and War Walkers, this is a psyker-dense castle that fuses layered Lethal Hits pressure with mobile vehicle fire — running either Armoured Warhost to give AELDARI VEHICLE units Assault on their ranged weapons or Seer Council to generate a Fate dice pool that fuels detachment Stratagems when the matching value is present. The plan is to park a durable wraith-and-warlock core on mid-board objectives while War Walkers push Assault-enabled shooting into anything that moves, stacking Lethal Hits sources to bleed through armour and elite infantry simultaneously. It punishes lists that rely on trading shots from static heavy platforms, since the Assault vehicle fire lets War Walkers shoot after advancing, maintaining threat range while the warlock screen denies easy angles. It cracks under concentrated alpha-strike pressure or elite melee that can collapse the castle before the Lethal Hits engine fully engages — at sub-50% wins, this build is clearly struggling to close games consistently.
609: Built around Custodian Guard, Vertus Praetors, Allarus Custodians, and Venatari Custodians riding inside transports, this is a mobile infantry brawler running the Might of the Moritoi detachment to push ADEPTUS CUSTODES WALKER units up the board faster with +2" Movement, +1 advance, and +1 charge, while Shield Host's Martial Ka'tah cycling keeps elite melee output flexible round to round. The plan is to deliver multiple elite infantry units into mid-table simultaneously, overwhelm contested objectives through sheer melee threat density, and grind opponents off scoring positions. It punishes slower gunlines that can't efficiently chew through high-save elite bodies before the transport wave hits home. However, lists that generate volume anti-tank early can strip the transports before delivery, leaving expensive infantry stranded and the engine stalled.
438: Built around Kastelan Robots managed by Cybernetica Datasmiths, Onager Dunecrawlers, and Belisarius Cawl as the central Tech-Priest anchor, this list splits between Lords of the Forge and Cohort Cybernetica detachments to stack survivability and board presence simultaneously. The plan is to park Kastelans on objectives using their boosted OC from Cohort Cybernetica while the Dunecrawler gunline and Kataphron Breachers grind through targets, with Tech-Priests protected by 4+ Invulnerable and 5+ Feel No Pain buying time to score progressively. It punishes slow or low-mobility lists that cannot contest multiple objectives simultaneously against high-OC, high-durability Robots anchoring the midfield. However, aggressive alpha-strike armies that can bypass or focus down the Datasmiths early — collapsing the Kastelan support structure before the gunline stabilizes — will expose how static and internally dependent this build truly is.
540: Built around Vindicators as the fire base, backed by Incursors, Sanguinary Guard, Land Speeders, Inceptors, and a jump pack Captain, this list blends a static demolisher core with fast-moving assault elements across multiple detachment configurations. The plan is to use Vindicators and skimming Land Speeders to crack armour and clear midfield while Sanguinary Guard and Inceptors threaten charges that, depending on detachment, gain bonus Attacks or wound re-rolls to finish off whatever the guns leave behind. It punishes slower, medium-density lists that can't simultaneously screen against deep-striking Inceptors and tank the Vindicator's demolisher cannon. A sub-50% win rate tells the story though — lists with durable long-range anti-tank can pick off the Vindicators early, and without that gunline pressure the melee threat alone lacks the teeth to close games.
584: Built around Militarum Tempestus Command Squads and Tempestus Scions supported by massed Cadian Recon, Krieg Engineers, and multiple heavy weapons squads, this is a high-volume gunline that floods the table with bodies and firepower across three interchangeable detachments. The plan is to deep strike Scions into scoring positions and punish movement with layered Orders boosting hit rerolls on ones, while heavy weapons squads grind through anything that tries to hold the midfield. It brutally punishes armies that need to close distance to fight, since the sheer volume of bodies and fire — especially Scions arriving with +1 to hit rolls when set up the same turn — makes midboard advances extremely costly. Concentrated elite melee threats that can alpha strike the Scions before they shoot, or fast units that screen out deep strike landing zones, can collapse the engine before it fires.
548: Built around Rogal Dorn Commanders, Hellhounds, Hippogriff AFVs, and Scout Sentinels supported by Tech-Priest Enginseers keeping vehicles in the fight, this is a Steel Hammer mechanised gunline that floods the table with armoured hulls. The win condition is sustained ranged attrition — Steel Hammer lets Squadron and Titanic units fire into engagements without penalty, meaning screens can't cuddle up to tanks to shut them down, and the build leverages that freedom to grind opposing armies off objectives through sheer volume of vehicle fire. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that lack the anti-tank overload to chew through the horde of hulls before the Enginseers repair them back to relevance. Heavy anti-armour spam that can drop multiple vehicles per turn cracks it open, since losing key damage platforms faster than the Enginseer can patch them collapses the entire attrition engine.
610: Built around Allarus Custodians, Vertus Praetors, and Custodian Guard supported by Witchseekers and Prosecutors, this is a transport-heavy midboard brawler that floods the table with elite, durable infantry delivered aggressively into the center. The win condition is positional dominance — use the high Objective Control of Custodian units to contest and hold midfield while Allarus and the Blade Champion delete priority targets in melee, with Witchseekers and Prosecutors providing psychic wound denial and action economy on the flanks. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that struggle to shift high-OC, high-toughness bodies from objectives without massed anti-tank or high-volume shooting. It cracks under anti-infantry overload and armies that can force it off objectives at range, since the list's elite pricing means losing even a handful of models collapses its board presence and OC math rapidly.
542: Built around Legionaries packed into Chaos Rhinos, Noise Marines, and Chaos Predator Destructors led by a Chaos Lord, this is a mechanised mid-table gunline with real anti-armour teeth. The plan is to drive Rhino transports onto objectives, unload Legionaries with Assault-enabled ranged weapons and improved AP from Renegade Raiders, and let Predator Destructors hammer armour while Noise Marines saturate infantry — scoring through presence and attrition rather than surgical strikes. It punishes slower gunline armies that can't contest mid-board, because the AP bonus on objectives turns even modest weapons into serious threats against anything holding ground. Anything with strong alpha-strike potential or durable deep-strike units can peel the Rhinos before they deliver, collapsing the whole engine before it gets rolling.
524: Built around Azrael, Deathwing Knights, Inner Circle Companions, and Lion El'Jonson anchoring a durable infantry core under Wrath of the Rock, which subtracts 1 from Wound rolls whenever an attacker's Strength exceeds the target's Toughness, making the entire Adeptus Astartes Infantry and Mounted battleline functionally tougher against the majority of weapons in the game. The plan is to grind through the midfield using layered, hard-to-wound elites while Scouts screen early and Intercessors hold secondaries, converting durability into sustained scoring rather than explosive burst damage. It punishes lists that lean on mid-Strength volume fire — the wound subtraction neuters the exact weapon bracket most armies spam — while transports push Knights and Companions into brawl range efficiently. However, true high-Strength anti-tank overload (weapons that already match or beat Toughness comfortably) bypasses the detachment entirely, and at 46% wins the list struggles to close games against faster, more explosive opposition.
471: Built around Knight Despoilers, a Chaos Cerastus Knight Atrapos, and War Dog Karnivores screened by Nurglings, Beasts of Nurgle, and Plaguebearers, this is a Infernal Lance list that leans hard into Nurgle daemon chaff to protect its heavy armour. The engine is the Malefic Surge: risk a Leadership test each Command phase to Empower your Knights, then drive layered lethal anti-armour firepower and melee into the opponent's expensive models while the daemon screen bleeds activations and contaminates objectives. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that struggle to chew through the daemon bubble before the Knights reach combat range and start deleting armoured targets. However, volume-fire horde lists or anything with consistent mortal wound output can drain the Knights through failed Leadership tests and screen attrition before the Malefic Surge payoff lands.
595: Built around Indomitor and Fortis Kill Teams, a Captain in Gravis Armour, and Deathwatch Terminators backed by Incursors and Infiltrators screening the midboard, this is a Black Spear Task Force list that leans hard into mixed-Toughness kill teams to artificially inflate durability — when wounds are resolved against a kill team containing models of different Toughness values, attackers must use the majority Toughness, making these units survive far more punishment than their raw statlines suggest. The plan is to push durable, hard-to-wound kill teams onto objectives while layered gunline output grinds opposing units off the table. It punishes lists built around a single dominant Strength bracket, since majority-Toughness resolution means no single wound roll is optimal against the mixed teams. It cracks open against true elite anti-armour spam or mass mortal-wound output that bypasses wound rolls entirely, circumventing the core defensive interaction.
570: Built around multiple Defilers, Mortarion, a Daemon Prince of Nurgle, and swarms of Chaos Spawn and Poxwalkers, this list runs either Virulent Vectorium or Paragons of Putrescence to lock down the mid-board with a wall of durable, contagion-spreading filth. The win condition is attrition through layered lethality — Mortarion and the Daemon Prince spread Contagion across multiple objectives while Defilers provide heavy fire support and Spawn flood flanks, grinding opponents down until they can't contest what the horde holds. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that struggle to out-clear sticky objective holders reinforced by Virulent Vectorium's persistent control ability. However, high-volume mortal wound output or strong alpha-strike lists can surgically remove Mortarion before his Contagion engine comes online, collapsing the whole cascade.
539: Built around Rotigus, a Great Unclean One, Beasts of Nurgle, and dense screens of Nurglings and Plaguebearers, this list runs Tallyband Summoners to cross-pollinate the Plague Legions and Death Guard halves — Nurgle's Gift onto the daemons, extended Contagion Range onto the mortals — creating a board-wide lethality bubble that rewards proximity and punishes enemies who have to push into it. The win condition is layered attrition: stack Contagion Range through Paragons of Putrescence and Beckoning Blight, flood midfield with cheap bodies, and grind opponents down through accumulated debuffs while scoring on objectives the enemy can't safely contest. It punishes low-model-count elite lists that must walk into the Contagion web and lack the volume to trade efficiently against a horde that replenishes pressure. It cracks against high-mobility gunlines that can kite outside 12" and delete key characters before the bubble fully assembles.
574: Built around a massive blob of Possessed supported by Abaddon, Fabius Bile, Chosen, and a Master of Possession, this is a horde-weight melee brawler that floods the midboard with durable, buffed infantry. The win condition is overwhelming individual objective zones through sheer body count and combat output — Abaddon anchors the kill chain while Fabius and the Master of Possession stack augmentations and buffs onto the Possessed to punch well above their base statline. It punishes lists that lack mass anti-infantry firepower, drowning them in bodies before they can strip the horde efficiently, with Mutilators providing a mobile anti-armour threat that forces awkward target priority. However, high-volume mortal wound output, blast weapons, or elite shooting that scales against large units cracks it open by collapsing the horde's volume advantage before it reaches combat.
575: Built around Hellions, Wyches, and a Succubus core, this list layers Exhibition of Slaughter's Lethal Hits on all Wych Cult melee attacks against non-Monsters and non-Vehicles with Skysplinter Assault's disembark-and-strike engine, granting Lance on melee weapons the turn units pile out of Venoms. The plan is to flood the midboard with fast skimmer-delivered infantry, disembark into combat with Lance-boosted, Lethal Hits-fueled melee swarms, and grind scoring through sheer body count while Scourges provide ranged pressure. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that struggle to clear hordes before the Wych Cult melee wave hits with full modifier stacking. However, heavy anti-horde shooting or durable Vehicle/Monster-heavy lists that resist Lethal Hits and can clear screens before disembarkation deny the entire kill chain.
541: Built around Warp Talons, a Chaos Lord with Jump Pack, and Raptors as the core assault engine, this list floods the board with HERETIC ASTARTES INFANTRY FLY units supported by Forgefiend gunline fire and Warpsmith tech. The win condition is a pressure loop: crack units below half-strength or force battle-shock early, then leverage re-roll hit mechanics on already-wounded targets to compound damage and snowball kills across multiple combats. It punishes slow, durable gunlines that bleed wounds gradually — the moment their key units dip below half-strength, the hit re-rolls turn trades into massacres. Against fast, elite alpha-strike lists that delete Warp Talons before the battle-shock loop activates, the engine stalls completely, leaving the list without its core damage amplification.
588: Built around Flawless Blades, Infractors, and a Lord Exultant riding Chaos Rhinos into the midfield, this is a transport-heavy melee swarm that weaponizes the charge. The engine is simple: Rhinos deliver infantry into charge range, triggering the detachment's charge bonus (Lethal Hits or Sustained Hits 1 on melee weapons) while Spectacle of Slaughter grants Flawless Blades Fights First, letting them win combat trades before the opponent can swing back. It punishes mid-density infantry lists badly — multiple Fights First units hitting with Lethal Hits or Sustained Hits 1 on the charge eats through medium-wound squads faster than they can respond. Against armies with strong overwatch, high-volume screens, or shooting that strips Rhinos before the charge lands, the whole delivery system collapses and the melee payoff never arrives.
572: Built around Aberrants, the Abominant, Biophagus, and Purestrain Genestealers flooding the midboard, this list runs Biosanctic Broodsurge to stack charge bonuses — every unit that crashes in on a charge gains +1 Attacks on all melee weapons, turning already-lethal blobs into a grinding kill machine. The win condition is layered lethality: screen the midboard with Neophyte Hybrids and Acolyte Hybrids, then avalanche the charge-buffed Aberrant core into whatever the opponent values most, scoring through sheer combat attrition and holding terrain with a durable horde. It punishes elite low-model armies catastrophically — a single buffed Aberrant unit charging into expensive infantry or monsters generates disproportionate returns that elite lists simply cannot trade back against. However, opponents who can alpha-strike or shoot out the charge threats before they engage, or who deny midboard positioning with strong screen-and-deny tools, can dismantle the engine before the charge bonuses ever fire.
581: Built around Subductor Squads and Inquisitorial Agents riding Chimeras, supported by Imperial Navy Breachers and Voidsmen-at-Arms under an Inquisitor's command, this list runs primarily in Imperialis Fleet. The plan is to advance a layered transport brick up the board, stacking lethal hits across multiple infantry blobs while Imperialis Fleet's Eliminate At All Costs focuses the entire army's firepower onto one priority target per turn, dismantling threats piece by piece. It punishes lists that rely on single durable centerpieces — that focused-fire mechanism turns any one unit into a delete target regardless of defensive buffs. However, the build's moderate win rate exposes its ceiling: armies that can strip transports early strand expensive infantry in the open, and anything with enough shooting range to engage before the brick closes distance can unpick it before the kill chain activates.
592: Built around Purifier Squads anchoring Hallowed Ground zones, Grand Master and bare Nemesis Dreadknights providing heavy punch, and Strike and Interceptor Squads doing the mobile legwork, this is a mid-board control list with Castellan Crowe leading the Purifier core. The plan is to extend Hallowed Ground out of your deployment zone by parking Purifiers on No Man's Land objectives, using that expanding sanctified footprint to dictate where the game is fought while Dreadknights and Interceptors apply lethal pressure across multiple threat vectors. It punishes slower, lower-mobility armies that cannot contest mid-board early, because the Purifier anchors make dislodging that objective hold progressively more costly as Hallowed Ground expands. Lists with aggressive deep strike or fast melee that can isolate and kill Purifiers before the Ground is established crack it open by collapsing the zone before it becomes self-sustaining.
591: Built around Paladin Squads as the centerpiece, supported by Nemesis Dreadknights, Strike Squads, Purifiers, and Interceptors across the Argent Assault and Banishers detachments, this is a mobile melee-psychic force with multiple threat vectors across the board. The engine is Argent Assault's wound-roll bonus kicking in when Paladins punch up into high-Toughness targets, layered with Banishers' Leadership-test mechanic granting either Sustained Hits 1 or a second selectable bonus to Psychic melee weapons each fight phase, compounding damage output through the kill chain. It punishes mid-range and slow armies that cannot clear multiple durable elite infantry blobs before the Paladins and Dreadknights close distance, with Interceptors and Psychic Celerity keeping pressure mobile and constant. Armies that can alpha-strike the Paladins off the board before Banishers triggers, or that ignore the Leadership test through high-Leadership denial or simply kill the unit first, collapse the primary wound-bonus engine entirely.
594: Built around Armiger Helverins and Warglaives supported by Knight Destriers, Paladins, and a Castellan, this list runs Gate Warden Lance as its primary detachment and supplements with Throne-Bonded Outriders to weaponize its Armigers. The gameplan is to anchor two objective markers as foundations, hold the defensive line with large-base Knights that are nearly impossible to budge, then flood the board with Bondsman-buffed Armigers whose ranged attacks gain Ignores Cover — punishing any opponent who tries to hide elite or expensive units behind terrain. It absolutely punishes slow, high-value melee armies that need to close ground, since those units walk into concentrated anti-armour fire before they can engage. Horde lists or anything generating overwhelming screening volume can dilute the Bondsman economy and force the big Knights to trade inefficiently.
568: Built around Kapricus Defenders as the core damage engine, supported by Sagitaurs, Kapricus Carriers, Hernkyn Yaegirs, and Ironkin Steeljacks, this list plays a layered midboard grind anchored in close-range firepower. The win condition runs through stacking YP via Needgaârd Oathband's per-kill income and Mercenary Oathband's Hostile Acquisition flip, funnelling that currency into compounding pressure while Hearthguard Covenant's wound-reroll-1 aura keeps the Defenders punching cleanly inside 9". It punishes lists that want to trade inefficiently in the midboard — skimmer mobility and transported infantry let it pick engagement angles and overwhelm slower gunlines through sheer kill-rate. Where it cracks is against alpha-strike armies or deep-strike threats that bypass its layered positioning before the YP engine comes online, leaving it without the resource pressure it needs to close games.
579: Built around multiple Doomsday Arks supported by Canoptek Wraiths, Ophydian Destroyers, and a Skorpekh Lord leading melee threats, all operating under Awakened Dynasty's +1 to Hit while a Character leads a unit. The plan is to castle the Arks in a fire-base while the Wraiths and Destroyers mobile-toolbox across the board, using the hit bonus to reliably punish anything the guns can reach while melee elements contest and clear midfield objectives. Awakened Dynasty's universal hit buff rewards stacking multiple attack vectors simultaneously, making it punishing against armies that spread thin or lack the volume to neutralize both the gunline and the aggressive melee packages at once. However, at under 50% win rate this list is crackable by fast alpha-strike armies that can close the Arks before they fire, or high-durability anti-armor builds that simply out-range the castle and strip it piecemeal.
580: Built around multiple Doomsday Arks providing sustained heavy firepower, Lokhust Heavy Destroyers as mobile anti-armour, and Flayed Ones plus Tomb Blades filling flexible harassment and board-control roles, this list functions as a toolbox gunline with meaningful threat range across the table. The engine is layered lethal output from the Arks anchoring backfield lanes while Lokhust Heavy Destroyers pressure high-value targets mid-board, with Ophydian Destroyers and Flayed Ones applying contact pressure to force opponents off objectives and deny scoring. It punishes static, high-toughness armies that clump — multiple Doomsday Arks concentrating fire into the same target bracket creates anti-tank overload that elite vehicle lists struggle to absorb. However, aggressive alpha-strike armies that close the distance fast can strip the screening layers and force the Arks to fire into melee-proximity chaff, collapsing the kill chain before it generates the damage needed to win the grind.
604: Built around massed Boyz, Beast Snagga Boyz, and Nobz delivered by Trukks, with Gretchin screening the backfield and a Warboss leading the charge, this is War Horde at its most literal. The plan is to crash melee-heavy units into the midboard early, leveraging War Horde's Sustained Hits 1 on all Ork melee weapons to generate extra hits at volume and grind opponents off objectives through sheer attrition. Follow Me Ladz on the Warboss amplifies the kill chain by pulling units forward, and the Trukk delivery system lets Nobz or Boyz threaten charges turn one before the opponent can establish a defensive line. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that can't trade efficiently into Sustained Hits 1 horde combat, but it cracks against shooting-heavy lists that delete Trukks before disembarkation and strand the melee payload in the open.
601: Built around massive blobs of Boyz supported by Painboys, Warbosses, and Bigbosses, this is an infantry-tide list that floods the midboard with bodies. The engine is simple but brutal: More Dakka! grants all Orks Infantry ranged attacks Assault, letting the horde shoot after advancing into engagement range, then crash into melee — and when the Waaagh! is active, those same attacks gain Sustained Hits 1, turning weight-of-fire into a genuine kill chain. It punishes elite low-model-count armies through sheer attrition, overwhelming threat saturation, and the near-impossibility of trading efficiently into 100+ wounds of Boyz. Anything that can thin the horde at range before the Waaagh! activates — heavy blast weapons, mass mortal wounds, or gunlines with strong screen-and-deny tools — can stall the advance before the melee payoff lands.
605: Built around Meganobz, Warboss characters, and Nobz riding inside Battlewagons, this is a Bully Boyz list that weaponizes the double-Waaagh! mechanic — calling it a second time exclusively for WARBOSS, NOBZ, and MEGANOBZ units to stack combat buffs and crash elite infantry blobs into the midboard. The scoring engine runs on delivering fully-buffed Meganobz and Nobz via Battlewagon transport, winning primary through sheer mid-table brawl dominance while Gretchin and Boyz screen and hold flanks. Tellyporta on 60% of lists adds a deep-strike threat vector that forces opponents to split attention, punishing gunlines and light-infantry chaff armies that can't disengage from locked combats. The list cracks against armies with consistent high-AP, high-damage anti-elite shooting that can strip the Battlewagons before the cargo delivers, leaving expensive Meganobz stranded on foot in the open.
600: Built around massed Boyz supported by Painboy buffs, a Warboss, and Ghazghkull Thraka as the hammer, this is a Freebooter Krew brawler that floods the midboard with cheap infantry screens anchored by Gretchin while its elite elements grind forward. The engine is the loot objective mechanic — designating a single objective each Command phase to farm double scoring — backed by Sustained Hits 1 on every attack from Infantry, Mounted, and Walker units, turning large Boyz blobs into a withering close-range kill chain. Kunnin' Hunta and Git-Spotter Squig sharpen key characters into precision hunting tools, punishing elite low-model-count armies that cannot trade efficiently against wave after wave of bodies soaking damage through Painboy support. Fragile to heavy anti-infantry volume fire that strips Boyz blobs before they reach combat range, leaving the scoring engine exposed and the loot objective undefendable.
602: Built around Ghazghkull, Gretchin screens, Big Meks with Shokk Attack Guns, Tankbustas, Flash Gitz, and Lootas riding in Trukks, this is a mid-table brawler with serious shooting teeth. The engine is Freebooter Krew's loot objective forcing opponents to contest a designated marker while Sustained Hits 1 stacks across the whole infantry line — when the Waaagh! is active, More Dakka!'s Assault attacks combine with that second Sustained Hits 1 trigger to flood the table with hits at a terrifying volume. It punishes static gunlines that can't close distance, drowning them in Dakka before they neutralise the Trukk delivery wave. Armies that strip transports early and force Orks to footslog into the midfield bleed the momentum this list needs to fight for the loot objective and convert kills into board control.
593: Built around Logan Grimnar, Arjac Rockfist, Wolf Guard Terminators, and a Captain in Terminator Armour stacked with support characters, this list runs Saga of the Great Wolf to cycle Hunting Packs — most critically Encircling Jaws for free re-rolls on Advances and Charges to keep the terminator brick threatening across the board. The plan is to deliver that melee core via transport infantry and skimmer fire support, using the Hunting Pack selection each turn to flex between aggression and accuracy as the game state demands. It punishes lower-durability midfield armies that can't absorb a multi-threat terminator delivery turn, especially when Grimnar's Mark and Skjald's Foretelling front-load consistency. A hard counter-drop or elite shooting that strips the transport layer before the brick lands leaves the list flat-footed and unable to reliably close the distance.
608: Built around multiple Forgefiends backed by a Defiler, Exalted Sorcerers on Discs, and cheap Chaos Spawn and Tzaangor screens, this list leans on Warpforged Cabal's re-roll engine — Thousand Sons Psykers positioned within 6" of each Vehicle to recycle hit, wound, and damage rolls on every shooting activation. The plan is to park Forgefiends in reliable mid-board fire lanes, use Psyker proximity to maximize vehicle damage output turn after turn, and let Ritual of Regeneration keep the Psyker support pieces healthy enough to maintain those auras. It punishes slow, durable armies that expect to weather early shooting — layered lethal re-rolls into anti-armour guns overload the damage mitigation of elite vehicle or monster lists. It cracks open against fast melee aggression and deep-strike denial threats that collapse the Psyker-to-Vehicle spacing, stripping the re-roll engine before it fires.
