597: Built around the Norn Emissary, Norn Assimilator, and Maleceptor as its core monsters, this list runs Talons of the Norn Queen to give both Norn variants Protean Purpose, letting them flex their role game-to-game, while Neurolictor and Screamer-Killers provide harassment and secondary threat angles. The plan is to leverage an adaptable multi-monster toolkit to contest mid-board objectives while Biovores chip away at screens and Neurolictor disrupts backfield play, accumulating primary points through monster bulk rather than any single kill chain. It punishes slower, tankier lists that can't answer multiple high-Toughness threats simultaneously, forcing anti-tank resources to split across several dangerous targets. Concentrated elite shooting or melee that can isolate and delete monsters one at a time cracks it open, since losing a key Norn variant early collapses the threat saturation the build depends on.
598: Built around Raveners, Hyperadapted Raveners, Trygons, and The Red Terror operating out of the Subterranean Assault detachment, which grants Mawloc and Trygon units the Burrower keyword and lets two Trygons take Enhancements and a Warlord designation. The plan is to surge a high-volume melee horde up the board — Burrowing Trygons emerging mid-table to anchor fights while Ravener blobs swarm objectives and grind through chaff with sheer model count. It punishes slow, static gunlines that can't reposition in time to handle simultaneous underground threats arriving from multiple angles. Durable elite armies with high-damage, high-AP output crack it open by stripping the Trygons before they can fight and leaving the Ravener swarms without a brawling anchor.
607: Built around Magnus the Red supported by Exalted Sorcerers, Rubric Marines in Chaos Rhinos, Mutalith Vortex Beasts, and Infernal Masters, this is a psychic-heavy midfield control list running primarily Grand Coven's rotating buffs — range extension, Ritual synergies, and regeneration layers across the force. The win condition is stacking layered psychic lethality through Eldritch Vortex of E'Taph and Umbralefic Crystal enhancements while Rhino-borne Rubrics contest mid-table and Magnus threatens high-value targets. It punishes static gunlines and low-mobility elite forces that cannot answer simultaneous threats across multiple threat vectors — the Mutalith and Magnus together demand two separate anti-monster answers. At roughly 50/50 win-rate, it struggles against aggressive alpha-strike lists that can isolate Magnus early before the psychic engine gets rolling.
485:
Built around Tyrannofexes, Exocrines, Norn Emissaries, and Maleceptors, this is a wall of Tyranid Monsters operating under Crusher Stampede, with Talons of the Norn Queen giving the Norn Emissary flexible Protean Purpose utility on top.

The plan is to park healthy full-strength Monsters on objectives — leveraging their +2 OC bonus from Crusher Stampede — while the Tyrannofex and Exocrine gunline dismantles enemy units at range, softening targets so damaged Monsters can swing back with boosted Hit and Wound rolls.

It punishes low-model-count elite armies that can't contest multiple high-OC footprints simultaneously while absorbing return fire poorly against T10+ statlines.

Cheap screen spam and alpha-strike lists that can rapidly drop Monsters below Starting Strength flip the detachment's OC engine against it, and without durable chaff of its own, it struggles to protect its big pieces from early attrition.
565: Built around Slaughterbound, Exalted Eightbound, and Eightbound backed by Forgefiend and Defiler daemon vehicles, this is a layered melee-and-armour brawler that floods the midboard with bodies and steel. The engine runs on forcing battle-shock rolls via Terror of Khorne at the start of each Fight phase, suppressing enemy units in combat while Brazen Fury surge moves pull Possessed-keyword units forward under fire to close distance faster than opponents can reset. It punishes slower midboard armies and elite infantry lists that can't generate enough shooting to clear Eightbound and daemon vehicles before they reach combat. Highly mobile screens and multiple armour threats fold when facing high-volume mortal wound output or dedicated anti-tank overload that can strip the daemon vehicles before Terror of Khorne ever triggers.
